Resolute Downgrades Annual Guidance Amid Continued Mali Disruptions
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Resolute Mining on Monday downgraded its production and cost guidance for 2026, citing a challenging operating environment in Mali that it said continues to impact underground mining, open-pit mining and sulfide processing.

The gold miner said it now expects 2026 gold production at its Syama mine to be between 150,000 troy ounces and 160,000 ounces, at a so-called all-in sustaining cost of between US$2,300 and US$2,400 an ounce.
As a result, annual group gold production is now estimated to be between 205,000 ounces and 225,000 ounces, at an all-in sustaining cost of between US$2,250 and US$2,350 an ounce.
Resolute previously forecast this year's group gold output to be toward the lower end of a 250,000-ounce to 275,000-ounce range, at a cost between US$2,000 and US$2,200 an ounce.

"Production at Syama has remained below plan due to the challenging operating environment in Mali," said the company. "These issues have continued to reduce ore availability, delay access to higher-grade ore sources and impact plant throughput and recovery."
Operational activities across the rest of Resolute's business remain on track, the company said.
